## Translation Yield: From Momentum to Displacement

A momentum configuration and the motion expressed from it are not the same statement. The first identifies what the particle carries. The second tells how that content becomes change of position. Translation yield enters between them.

For a chosen orientation $\hat{k}$, the shell readings preserve the signed directional component in positive form,

$$
p_k^\pm=M(p)\pm\frac12p_k,
$$

with the comparison identities

$$
M(p)=\frac{p_k^++p_k^-}{2},
\qquad
p_k=p_k^+-p_k^-.
$$

These identities display the symmetric core magnitude and the signed directional asymmetry. By the time the expansion engine is applied, that momentum configuration—and therefore $M(p)$ and $p_k$—has already been identified.

The inertial translation rule reads the signed fraction $p_k/M(p)$ as directed motion. Translation yield modifies that rule downstream:

$$
\boxed{
\dot x_k(t)=\chi(t)c\frac{p_k}{M(p)}
}.
$$

Each factor has one job. The ratio $p_k/M(p)$ gives the fraction of the particle's core momentum expressed along the selected direction. Its sign fixes the sense of translation relative to $\hat{k}$. The constant $c$ supplies the intrinsic local propagation scale. The factor $\chi(t)$ gives the displacement yielded by the spatial background at that epoch.

The limiting checks are immediate. When $\chi=1$, the inertial translation rule is recovered. When $p_k=0$, there is no translation along $\hat{k}$. Reversing the orientation reverses the signs of both $p_k$ and $\dot x_k$ without changing $M(p)$. For forward lightlike propagation, $p_k/M(p)=1$, so the map becomes $\dot x=\chi c$.

A larger value of $\chi$ therefore means more displacement from the same directed momentum fraction. A smaller value means less. What changes is the result of the translation map, not the momentum fed into it.

This separation protects the conservation structure. Translation yield does not rescale

$$
p_f,\quad \vec p,\quad p,\quad p_k,\quad p_k^\pm,\quad\text{or}\quad M(p).
$$

It does not appear inside ADMC, and it does not drain bosic momentum during propagation. It also does not replace the $c$ appearing in intrinsic relations such as $p_f=m_0c$. The cosmological dependence belongs to the complete expression $\chi(t)c$ in the displacement map, not to a second fundamental light constant.

The physical order is consequently precise:

$$
\text{momentum configuration}
\longrightarrow
\frac{p_k}{M(p)}
\longrightarrow
\chi(t)c\frac{p_k}{M(p)}
\longrightarrow
\text{displacement}.
$$

Space expansion enters at the third step. The next question is what this rule means for a light signal that propagates through many successive yield states.
